content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 14 and 30. Supplemental: SEI ATAM and Views and Beyond. This unit focuses on architecture evaluation.

Architecture evaluation asks whether the architecture is fit for its intended purpose. Scenario-based methods such as ATAM use stakeholder scenarios to uncover risks, sensitivity points, tradeoffs, and non-risks.
Evaluation does not require perfect certainty. It creates enough shared evidence to improve decisions, reduce unknowns, and make risks explicit before they become expensive.
Studio: run a mini evaluation on one design decision using three scenarios and identify one risk, one tradeoff, and one follow-up experiment.

concepts.name: Architecture evaluation
concepts.description: The assessment of whether an architecture satisfies important concerns, scenarios, constraints, and quality goals.

concepts.name: ATAM
concepts.description: Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method, a structured scenario-based method for analyzing architectural risks and tradeoffs.

concepts.name: Sensitivity point
concepts.description: An architectural decision or parameter where small changes can strongly affect a quality attribute.

concepts.name: Tradeoff point
concepts.description: An architectural decision that affects multiple quality attributes in competing ways.
